scope: Shared scene/take/sequence WebM canvas frame admission reliability; sequence trimming model unchanged

checks.command: node --check src/export.js; node --check tests/export-capture.test.js; node --check tests/export-bounds.test.js; node --check tests/lifecycle.test.js

firstActualFailure.classification: Existing automatic capture had no manual request lifecycle or two-stream fallback. Four assertions failed before awaited completion; two failures reached unchanged11s watchdog instead of expected manual failure. Two abandoned baseline test promises produced retained asynchronous timeout warnings; test cleanup now stops any still-owned fake recorder.

capturePolicy.initial: draw0, admit manual stream, start native recorder, request initial frame
capturePolicy.cadence: On genuine RAF draws request only when elapsed since last request >=1000/30ms. Do not synthesize catch-up frames.
capturePolicy.terminal: If exact clamped End draw is too soon, keep native recording until the next genuine eligible RAF draw requests End, then stop. The duration+10s deadline remains.
capturePolicy.time: Draw evaluates Math.min(duration,(rafTimestamp-started)/1000); no changed source offset or frame clock.
capturePolicy.fallback: If requestFrame is unavailable, stop every probe track before one captureStream30 admission, rechecking abort between admissions. Request/encoder failures do not fallback.

compatibilityEdits.change: Controlled streams now expose the same owned track through getTracks/getVideoTracks with a requestFrame method. All original cleanup counts and failure assertions retained.

nativeEvidence.status: Root-coordinated final unmodified native acceptance pending; this producer did not launch browser tests.
nativeEvidence.priorRootReportedScratch: Root reported same original60s maximum gate accepted1063 decodedframes,5016553bytes,40pixel samples/endpoints/restart. This scratch result motivates the repair and is not a claim of this exact final source gate.

limitations: Requested frame cadence is not a guarantee of encoded FPS or every authored cut being encoded.
Browser rendering/encoding can drop frames; maximum native decoding is a separate acceptance gate.
Automatic30Hz fallback preserves compatibility but has not acquired a new frame-density guarantee.
